questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been on exchange once before during my Bachelor's degree, which was an amazing experience. However, I didn't learn quite what I expected at the university. I learned many other things and lived a life that I look back on with much fondness, but I really wanted this exchange to be all about learning new things and challenging myself academically. This was the main reason for my exchange at McGill. Secondly, I wanted to study across the Atlantic. I wanted to go further away and experience something very different. I wanted to study somewhere with an interesting cultural life and beautiful nature — Montréal was perfect for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wish that I had spent a bit less time worrying about my studies. I learned so much, but I didn't quite feel like I had the time and energy to explore everything that I wanted to explore in Montréal and Canada.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. We received many e-mails and I went to a few online 'onboarding' seminars. Registering for classes was still a bit difficult, but it worked out in the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.answer: Guidance counselors.

questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register as soon as possible.

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 400-level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They treat you a bit more like Danish High School Students. There is a lot of homework and assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMS 492 – Power, Difference and Justice
ENGL 441 – Special Topics in Canadian Cultural Studies
COMS 400 – Critical Theory Seminar
ENGL 460 – Studies in Literary Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all, but especially COMS 400 and COMS 492. We learned to think about society in new and different ways. Asking questions about the life and society, rethinking what we accept as given. It was fascinating.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food at the grocery stores was more expensive, the coffee at cafés was less.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were all kinds of sports activities available and a gym. I was a part of the outdoor club and the ski club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend the ski club and outdoor club. It was great in the winter semester, if you like to go outside and experience nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and drive to the mountains or 'nearby' cities – Quebec City and Toronto etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It's quite a European city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet people in class and at the after school clubs. It's the easiest.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier. Most people speak French.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The liveliness of the city and the friendliness of the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Be prepared for challenging classes and spending lots of time on studying. 2. Don't study too hard and forget to explore the city. 3. Learn the language if you have time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends and challenging myself academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing everything that I wanted and needed to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
